summary.headline: Last year's profit was an accounting reversal; the solar contracts are running down
summary.text: LAUGFS Power PLC (LPL.N0000 voting, LPL.X0000 non-voting) owns solar plants at Hambantota and Embilipitiya and small hydro plants, selling all its power to the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB). Its reported profit of Rs 461mn for the year to March 2026 (EPS Rs 1.19) came almost entirely from reversing Rs 544mn of earlier impairments; without that it lost money, as generation fell 14%. The six months to September 2026 were better: revenue up 17% and profit Rs 87mn (EPS Rs 0.23), helped by the hydro plants. But the main solar contracts have only about ten years left, the CEB owes it about Rs 1.07bn, and it pays no dividend. At Rs 10.30 (voting, 30 September; check the live price) the share is 1.4x its NAV of Rs 7.17. A cash-flow valuation of the remaining contracts and a NAV check put fair value at about Rs 5.00, so the price is about double that. I'd buy at up to about Rs 4.25 and treat under Rs 3.75 as a strong buy.

fullText:
Summary: LAUGFS Power PLC (LPL.N0000 voting, LPL.X0000 non-voting) owns solar plants at Hambantota and Embilipitiya and small hydro plants, selling all its power to the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB). Its reported profit of Rs 461mn for the year to March 2026 (EPS Rs 1.19) came almost entirely from reversing Rs 544mn of earlier impairments; without that it lost money, as generation fell 14%. The six months to September 2026 were better: revenue up 17% and profit Rs 87mn (EPS Rs 0.23), helped by the hydro plants. But the main solar contracts have only about ten years left, the CEB owes it about Rs 1.07bn, and it pays no dividend. At Rs 10.30 (voting, 30 September; check the live price) the share is 1.4x its NAV of Rs 7.17. A cash-flow valuation of the remaining contracts and a NAV check put fair value at about Rs 5.00, so the price is about double that. I'd buy at up to about Rs 4.25 and treat under Rs 3.75 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 10.30 voting, Rs 8.80 non-voting (last traded, 30 September 2026). Please check them live. In July–September 2026 the voting share traded between Rs 10.00 and Rs 11.60; a year earlier it was Rs 15.80.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 480mn (up 17%), operating profit Rs 184mn (Rs 99mn), profit Rs 87mn (Rs 23mn), EPS Rs 0.23 (Rs 0.06). Hydro revenue Rs 91mn (Rs 22mn), solar Rs 389mn (Rs 387mn). EBITDA about Rs 328mn.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 765mn (down 15%), generation 35.2 GWh (down 14%), profit Rs 461mn including a Rs 544mn impairment reversal, EPS Rs 1.19. Without the reversal, a loss of about Rs 84mn.
NAV Rs 7.17 a share (September 2026). Net debt about Rs 1.55bn. 387 million shares. LAUGFS Holdings owns 74% of the voting shares.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Cash-flow DCF | 2.3 | 4.6 | 6.6 | 4.3
NAV multiple | 4.3 | 5.7 | 7.2 | 5.6
Average | 3.3 | 5.2 | 6.9 | 5.0
Fair value about Rs 5.00 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull). Buy at up to Rs 4.25 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 3.75 (25% below).

Assumptions
Free cash flow (EBITDA less tax and upkeep) of Rs 430 / 520 / 600mn a year for the roughly ten years left on the solar contracts, discounted at 17% / 15% / 13.5%. The hydro plants add Rs 50 / 100 / 100mn a year for years 11–20. Overdue CEB receivables count for Rs 0.40 / 0.60 / 0.75bn. NAV cross-check at 0.6 / 0.8 / 1.0 times.

What stands out
- Last year's profit was an accounting write-back, not cash.
- The plants are wasting assets: once the contracts end, tariffs and output after that are unknown.
- The CEB owes it more than a year's revenue.
- Debt is moderate (net debt about half of equity).

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 5.00, 150 up to Rs 4.25, 150 up to Rs 3.75: average about Rs 4.40, about Rs 2,200 in total. Rs 4.25 needs a fall of about 59%, so it isn't likely soon.

What would change my view
Higher: contracts extended at good tariffs, the CEB paying up, new plants at good returns, hydro output staying high.
Lower: falling generation, later CEB payments or tariff cuts, another impairment, money tied up with group companies.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (debt): avoid for now.
